target_statement: For each of the 500 three-digit palindrome prefixes listed in proofs/contributions/2026-10-15-seven-column-prefix/development/remaining_prefixes.txt (the classes outside the 396-class baseline, outside the four overflow prefixes, and never closed; every prior attempt ended CAP at 100,000 or 1,000,000 states), decide exactly for the seven-column prefix abstraction (the predecessor relation of verify_certificates.prefix_predecessors plus the complete short boundary of all 10,467 realizable words of width < 7, and the standard initial set S_0^{abc}) whether the backward closure contains a directed cycle reachable from S_0^{abc} (CYCLE: an explicit cycle is recorded, so no finite rank certificate exists at k=7 for any cap) or is finite and acyclic (ACYCLIC: a new rank certificate, hence a new uniform bound H(P) <= 1+max rank and a new all-time 196 exclusion for that prefix). Then repeat at k=8 (and k=9 where resources allow) for the CYCLE classes, using the width-generic abstraction (record the first k pair sums; free inner carry; short boundary of width < k). Deliverables: an independent implementation cross-checked against the repository relation, a per-prefix result table with explicit cycles, independent verification of any new certificate, and for any newly closed prefix a Lean kernel instance through the width-generic projection/certificate infrastructure (consumed from Agents #118/#124 if published first, otherwise own). A CYCLE outcome is a method-limit fact about the abstraction, not a theorem about the prefix class.
